en: Preface to the Hundred Questions on Penetrating the Profundity:
I have heard that the orthodox lineage of the Spirit Mountain was personally received by Kāśyapa, and the true wind of Shaoshi was directly transmitted by Shen Guang.
Since the sixth patriarch and through the five schools, the thunder of the Dharma has resounded throughout the Central Plains, and the light of the Buddha’s sun has flowed into the Imperial Gardens.

There have been those among his descendants who have cultivated the grasses [of the lineage]. Yuan Tong composed the *Hundred Questions* to inspire his disciples, elucidating the single mind and widely upholding the ancestral Way.
His words are concise and appropriate; their meaning is profound and subtle. How could they be sought through mere paper? How could they be discerned through the corners of the mouth?
Were one not a person of great capacity, it would be difficult to grasp such a vast mechanism. At that time, no such person was encountered.

It was only after several days that I encountered the author. Thus, when the Venerable Master Wansong resided at the Mahābodhi Hermitage, he employed the supernatural power of samādhi and right reception;
amidst his transmission of the Dharma and his leisure from maintaining the community, he answered the aforementioned hundred questions in the space of a finger-snap.
He guides the deluded masses of later generations toward the present moment. His eyes possess sinews; Linji’s function is free and easy, attaining the sublime.

His tongue has no bone; Yunmen’s words meet the source from every direction. He does not restrict himself to the partial or the perfect regarding the root of awakening, nor is he fixed upon gain or loss at Qingliang.
To study many words is merely to know how to exhaust one's effort; it is like a person bowing—his feet endure the fatigue, yet behind his head he possesses another pair of tongs.

Hammer. The original text of the *Jihben* (The Root of the Tongue) exists separately; the question of Yuan-tong and the instruction of Wan-song may indeed be called perfect. Therefore, I have not discarded them.

Following the precedent of Chen-lun, I have relied upon this record to compose these superficial words. Not only do they fail to benefit the Chan lineage, but I also risk being improperly presumptuous in trespassing upon the domain of the Patriarchs.
When the verses were more than half-finished, Master Zong-hui had already begun his chanting; by the time the recording was completed, [the work was fully realized].
Later, Yongshu was able to compose verses in response to them, and eventually this reached the two elders, causing them to be ridiculed by those in all quarters.

To understand the matter from beginning to end, one must read it with a wild spirit and provide the following annotations: "Idle in the monastic groves for several autumns, there has been no means to thoroughly investigate the teachings of our school.
Foolish and ignorant as I am, I feel ashamed that my days have passed in vain; I can only bear to patch a fox’s tail onto a sable robe. Thus, I briefly set forth this intention.
Preface: Written by Linquan Xian Dao of Longyan on the second day before the Qixi Festival.
"One Hundred Questions on Penetrating the Profundities" was established as a set of inquiries by the Great Chan Master Yuan Tong of Yuxi Tongxuan Hermitage.
Wansong Heshang of Mahābodhi Aranya respectfully responds to the verse by the Elder Linquan of Longyan;
carved by the Daoist Shengsheng of Huating.
Question: Practicing the profound is still traversing rugged terrain. What is the level ground? Answer: East, west, south, and north. Verse:
East, west, south, and north; thorns that pierce the heavens. Stone figures with feet submerged; there is no need for laborious effort.
Yet one must further penetrate yet another layer of barriers. Only when moving freely in all directions can one finally cast off entanglements.
Question: "The most profound and mysterious state must also be criticized. Tell me, what fault is there? Answer: "The offense shall not be punished with excessive severity. Verse:
"The offense shall not be punished with excessive severity; Idle supervision of the *tāla* palm. Before a word is even spoken, one has already erred;
How much more so when shifting moods and perversities arise? A-he-he! What is the use of contending over the profound and the most profound?"
Question: "A single flower [covers] ten billion lands; tell me, where is that single flower? Answer: "Even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
Verse: Even where there is no elegance, there is elegance; a stemless flower blooms atop an iron tree. Clever Chan practitioners, look up with keen eyes;
this is not like the spring colors that charm the imperial capital.
Question: The heavens are like fire and the summer rains are like boiling water. At such a time, how can one avoid them? Answer:
Before the main mountain, behind the supporting mountain. Verse: Before the main mountain, behind the supporting mountain; at midday, facing south, look for the Northern Dipper.
Amidst the surging heat of summer, let time flow on; ultimately, it cannot invade the Elder of Formlessness. Question:
"If the great ocean were used as ink and Mount Sumeru as a brush, tell me, what would be written? Answer: "The Hundred Questions of Penetrating Mystery. Verse:
The Hundred Questions of Penetrating Mystery do not adhere to fixed prosody; whether granting or revoking, they are applied according to the occasion, each finding its proper place. There is...
Someone asked me, "What are you doing? I replied, "I am observing the shifting movements of patterns as they unfold.
He asked, "When one contemplates flowers in the garden, one awakens to True Suchness (Tathatā). Now, as you contemplate these flowers, is there anyone who has awakened to the True?"
Answer: "I ask the Lord of the East, and he knows not. Verse: "I ask the Lord of the East, and he knows not. What indeed is this matter of not knowing?
Only when deaf at the nostrils can one truly listen; only when blind as the eyebrows can one truly perceive."
Question: "All things undergo transformation; is there anything that does not transform? Answer: "Dwelling on the shore, one confuses the way. Verse: Dwelling on the shore, one confuses the way;
true speech is indeed true. The dragon tower has no overnight guests; the phoenix pavilion has court ministers. Grasp the essential meaning within the profound mystery;
enough with boasting about the dust beneath your feet. If you wish to exhaustively reach the point of intimacy, when the nine realms are exhausted, you will meet it again.
Spring. Question: "The four seasons undergo change; is there anything that does not change? Answer: "Cold in spring, heat in autumn. Verse: Cold in spring, heat in autumn;
year after year, no difference. The azure sea is but a speck of dust; the red furnace is but a flake of snow. Leaves remaining after the frost.
The fallen tree is originally at rest; after the rain has passed and the clouds have gathered, the sky becomes even more pure.
Question: "One seeks a teacher and visits the Way for the purpose of practicing Chan. But how does one practice Chan? Answer: "I have long admired the fragrance of the Way. Verse:
Long admired the fragrance of the Way, Where principle and phenomena are both fused. Every word is Prajñā; Every thing is perfect penetration. Its...
Or perhaps you have missed the pivotal phrase; for now, go to Songyang and question the Patriarch.
Question: "Where does the water buffalo of Mount Huai graze? Answer: "In the lush green places. Verse:
The crow sits in the deep green; even by rubbing one’s forehead, it would be difficult to glimpse him. If you intend to ask further how this is so, the hawk has already flown off to Silla.
The cowherd boy sings loudly as he returns under the moon; the rope on his nose has snapped, and from the start there was no basis for it. HŪṂ.
Question: Deshan was a descendant of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; why did he beat them even when a Buddha came and even when a Patriarch came? Answer: Out of fear of negligence. Verse:
Out of fear of negligence, he has long been accustomed to the monastic groves. Knowing gratitude and repaying kindness, his heart-mind is uninterrupted.
Yunmen’s true command he is willing to uphold; take it for granted that the rivers will clear and the seas will be calm.
Question: Linji was a scion of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; why did he shout when a Buddha came and also shout when a Patriarch came? Answer:
It was precisely because a Buddha had come and a Patriarch had come. Verse: When a Buddha comes and a Patriarch comes, one must strictly avoid guessing wildly.
I shall now, for your sake, blast it open with ten characters. If you have not yet understood the true message, listen further to the sudden thunder shaking the nine realms.
"Ha! Question: Zhaozhou pointed at the cypress; Śākyamuni held up a flower. Tell me, are they the same or different? Answer: He held up two fingers. Verse:
Holding up two fingers, he established the fundamental principles and transmitted the total grasp—nothing more. To try to create complications beyond this point is truly exhausting.
Branches. Do not mistake floating splendor for wild blossoms.
Question: "Who can enjoy the place where Dongshan has neither cold nor heat? Answer: "The stone statue of Jiazhou. Verse:
The stone statue of Jia Prefecture has eyebrows arching over its eyes, filling the void of space. Impartial and without faction, it possesses many ways to delight the mind and bring joy;
what need is there to offer worship with flowers in one's mouth?
Question: One must directly ascend to the wondrous high peak. But how does one ascend that wondrous high peak? Answer: It is a laborious matter of great importance. Verse:
It is a laborious matter of great importance; it is the person who manipulates it. Grasping the "blowing-hair" sword with skill, the ten thousand realms are unified.
Without involving even a speck of dust, one traverses the great chiliocosm. One must know that where there is no function, true function is realized.
Question: "Luminosity and ignorance are non-dual in their nature. What is this non-dual nature? Answer:

"At dawn, nothing is revealed. Verse: At dawn, nothing is revealed; the dragon’s cry mingles with the lingering mist. In speech, one must avoid total completion; in the pivot of action, one prizes mutual interplay.
The sun’s orb is about to cast its light over the vast blue sea, yet it is needlessly obstructed by thin mist.
Question: "To leap directly into the stage of the Tathāgata—how do you explain the principle of this 'leaping'?

Answer: "The kind who carry water-jars on their shoulders. Verse: The kind who carry water-jars on their shoulders—how could they value a wise plan? Only then will one believe that pure greed leads to eternal bliss.
Knowing that turbid wealth brings much anxiety—[but, but, but]—one should seek a place of retreat and find it.
Question: Prajñā is non-knowing; why then is there nothing it does not know? Answer: Do not slander others. Verse: Do not slander others.
Skillful speech is not as good as speaking directly. If one can simply bring words to an end in profound mystery, one will see that the mind is not something fabricated.
Utterly still and naturally at ease, one trusts in things as they are; the fallen leaves before the steps are swept away by the wind.
Question: "Arranged beneath a bright window—tell me, what was it that was arranged? Answer: "The one who arrived just now. Verse:
The one who arrived just now, Mysteriously penetrating the profound and abstruse. Holding the cable while releasing the boat, Measuring the head to buy a hat.
Had it not been for the Buddha-Sun revealing his breast, Who could have entered the gateway of the Jia-ling school?
Question: "Though Chang'an is bustling, my country is at peace. What is this 'my country'? Answer: "Right in the midst of the bustle. Verse:

Right in the midst of the bustle, the enlightened master is free from obstruction; sitting and watching the clamor and stillness, the rise and fall, he holds the universe in his grasp, manifesting the holy age.
Question: Before Kāśyapa Mātanga arrived in this land, was there already the Teaching? Answer: I shall answer when you have attained "non-waiting.
Verse: When you have attained non-waiting, it is the Way; it is like a probing rod or a shadow-grass. Before the steps of the White Horse [Temple], he distinguished the coarse from the fine.
The numinous texts on palm leaves transcend past and present; do not give rise to anxiety and delusion by following words and phrases.
Question: Before Bodhidharma came to this land, was there still Chan? Answer: I shall speak when it exists. Verse:
When it exists, I shall speak; the sound and light are vast and rolling. Do not engage in false deliberation; cease seeking elsewhere. Cease seeking!
The tips of the willow branches ultimately have no jujubes.
Question: Why is the bottomless boat solid and leak-proof? Answer: It is cast from raw iron. Verse:
Cast from raw iron, it is neither heavy nor light; free from outflows and firm, it moves freely in all directions.
Without encountering waves, it roams the ocean of nature; in this world of five turbidities, it delivers sentient beings.
Question: "The Salt Official’s rhinoceros fan was entrusted to such a person as you. Answer: "I have already received your great kindness. Verse:
"I have already received your great kindness; these words may be remembered. When mouths open to face one another, how can there be room for deliberation?
In stillness, the bright moon hangs in the sky; In movement, the clear breeze pervades the earth."
Question: "Zhaozhou’s seven-pound hempen robe has been worn for many years; has it ever become tattered? Answer:
"Each time it is brought forth, it is fresh. Verse: Each time it is brought forth, it is fresh; taken up at hand, its use is most intimate.
Having been handled for one hundred and twenty years, even until now it remains inseparable from the body.
Question: When the clay ox roars at the moon, what kind of person can hear it? Answer: A leper’s eyebrows. Verse: A leper’s eyebrows indeed know how to hear;
Sumeru is startled awake and rides the clouds at night. One who knows the sound need not raise it again and again.
Eight *liang* clearly make half a *jin*.
Question: "The wooden horse neighs; who can understand its sound? Answer: "In vain you wipe your eyes. Verse: "In vain you wipe your eyes as you listen to the void;
The myriad sounds arise, yet they are fundamentally still. To examine the principle and hear the tone, do not waste your effort. Rain.
The remaining peaks remain as green as before, according to their former count.
Question: "A three-legged donkey trots about, prancing its hooves; tell me, how much ground does it travel in a day? Answer: "Do not run about recklessly."
Verse: Do not run about in confusion. Who does not have the talk of "falling into the weeds"? Cease further making a special issue of asking about your future prospects;
to deliberate and calculate constitutes a fault.
Question: "The hornless iron ox sleeps at Shaoshi; tell me, what use is there in this? Answer: "The humble one is unmoving and honored.
Verse: The humble one is unmoving and honored; the principle must be preserved. Below cannot fathom above—who would dare to debate it?
A ground beyond yin and yang, not subject to worldly involvement. The fabricated farmer vainly breaks his spirit.
Question: Although one has attained the Buddha-way, one does not abandon the gate of causes. Tell me, why is it so? Answer: It is threaded all at once. Verse:
Threaded all at once—how many complications! Think it over minutely; deliberate upon it thoroughly.
[But] merely conjecturing: "The black is the cold crow; the white is the crane. Question:
Since the Buddhas do not appear in the world, why did they nevertheless take birth in royal palaces? Answer: The green mountains constantly lift their feet. Verse:
The green mountains constantly lift their feet; even the Five Eyes would find them difficult to gaze upon. It is not that there is no great protection; it is because they are not [ordinary].
Identical to the mundane world. Identical to the mundane world. Transversely and vertically within desire, yet free from desire. Question:
If there is likewise no nirvana, why did he instead pass away at the Twin Trees?

Answer: The white sun does not shift its wheel. Verse: The white sun does not shift its wheel; it secretly communicates the spring beyond the kalpas. Do not greedily seek dawn and dusk, lest you obscure [the truth].
The person of original nature. The person of original nature dwells everywhere amidst the dust of the senses yet remains unstained by that dust.

Question: When Bodhidharma came from the West, he did not establish reliance on words and letters. Why then do you say that the *Vajracchedikā* and the *Laṅkāvatāra* are the essentials of our own mind?
Answer: It is precisely because of these essentials of the mind. Verse: Relying on these essentials of the mind, cut off all the profound and subtle; suddenly penetrate Zen.
The Barrier. A single aperture piercing through heaven— Who would have known that the old blue-eyed barbarian monk Still provokes the laughter of bystanders to this day?
Question: When the Second Patriarch sought his mind and found it was ultimately unattainable, why did [Bodhidharma] instead say, "I am merely tuning my own mind;

it is no concern of yours"? Answer: Do not meddle in affairs that are none of your business. Verse: Do not meddle in affairs that are none of your business. It is much like cutting what is long to patch over what is short. Three.
The stars, fragments, and moon have no inherent form; why trouble yourself by creating such rare wonder? Question:
The *Prajñāpāramitā* speaks of twenty kinds of emptiness. How does one discern among them? Answer: Neither too many nor too few. Verse:
Neither too many nor too few, it is clear and manifest. As the Third Patriarch said: "All people can understand this. The Ultimate Way is not difficult.
One phrase of intimacy: the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands is difficult for demons to disturb. Question:

Are the four marks of the Vajra and the four marks of the Perfect Enlightenment the same or different? Answer: It is like treating a disease by binding it from afar rather than applying moxibustion directly.
Verse: Tying up the horse while it grazes away from the fire—Old Lu holds the sovereign authority. Whether to grant or withhold depends on the moment; all you people, watch your own lives!
Iron cavalry and Zen monks, there is no need to contend; lately, the four seas have been as clear as a mirror.
Question: Among the twenty-five perfect penetrations (*vishuddhi*) of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, which one is the most intimate? Answer: A hospitable host has no estranged companions. Verse:
A hospitable host has no estranged companions; there is no need for further deliberation. The South Mountain and the North Mountain share a momentum that rivals the great heavens.
The bright moon and the dark clouds represent the two halves of the human masses—those who love and those who hate. Let the beautiful and the ugly be distinguished by others; as for my Way...
"One thread runs through them all. Question:
"It is easy to climb higher step by step; where is the highest point? Answer: "At the bottom of the great ocean. Verse:
At the bottom of the great ocean, who can compare with the Patriarchs? It is just like another peak—no more than half a meter apart.
Question: It is difficult to let go of the mind. Who is the person who has let go? Answer: Take it away. Verse:
"Take it away" is the most intimate point of Zhaozhou’s teaching. Though the bowl is filled, there is not a single thing within.
Do not follow after deluded thoughts and give rise to anxiety.
Question: "Who can penetrate Yangqi’s diamond circle? Answer: "Pass. Verse: "Pass. These pivotal points are as vast as heaven;
even the flash of lightning or a spark from flint is too slow to perceive them. One cannot avoid being personally scrutinized and exposed by them."
Question: "Who can swallow Yangqi’s chestnut thorn? Answer: "Liao. Verse: "Liao! His wondrous functioning and spiritual powers are no small matter;
the Buddha hall and the lantern accommodate one another. At this moment, who knows what this means?"
Question: Is there anyone who can pass through Huanglong’s Three Barriers? Answer: Unless it be the Master himself. Verse: Unless it be the Master himself;
in the practice of benevolence, one does not yield. A model for ten thousand ages, a standard for the ten directions. As for the Buddha’s hand and the donkey’s feet—why seek them elsewhere?
As for the conditions of self and other—these must be realized within oneself.
Question: [The Master] lets out a shout and says, "Tell me, is this the guest or the host? Answer: "Guest and host are clearly distinct. Verse:
At that time, the illumination and function were deployed; the treasury of the true Dharma-eye was extinguished by the blind donkey. Guest and host interpenetrate—the kung-an of the highest vehicle.
For those who know the sound, there is no need for further discernment.
Question: [The Master] held up the whisk and said, "I have finished expounding Chan for you; how do you understand this? Answer:
"Today, I am not at my ease. Verse: "Today, I am not at my ease; It is much like withdrawing troops while still engaging in battle.
Even if the Great Tang were shattered, it would be difficult to find; One only desires that the Master open a single thread of passage."
Question: Holding up his staff, he asked, "Is there anyone who can deliver a turning phrase upon the tip of this staff?
Answer: "The Master is advanced in years. Verse: In your venerable age, wondrous words transcend the ordinary mind; Without raising a blade, you settle all in Great Peace.
The purple swallow and the yellow oriole speak with such clever tongues, Yet one must know that the Great Sound is truly the sound of rarity.
Question: A single circular mark is drawn, and it is said, "The Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs are all contained within this.
How do you understand this? Answer: It is my good fortune from past lives. Verse: It is my good fortune from past lives; the sun is warm and the moon is cool.
The four seas have withdrawn their waves; heaven and earth are solemn and still. Even Master Qin was deluded by Master Ma; even until now, he has not yet awakened.
The Master asked, pointing a finger at the empty space: "Tell me, what does this single point clarify?
He replied, "Gui-zong is still here. Verse: "Gui-zong is still here; two colors, one match. On this side there is no hindrance; on that side..."
The margins are unobstructed. Record these eight dharmas forever and examine them well. In years past, a predecessor once downloaded them. Question:
"Do you recognize that person who does not step outside the door when walking, nor occupy the hall when sitting?

Answer: "A short-tailed dragon from the Cangzhou marsh. Verse: A short-tailed dragon from the Cangzhou marsh, Twisting and turning like a pine in winter cold. It does not borrow the brush of Lord Ye Gong.
Better to be confined by Ge’s staff than to leave no trace in the hall; yet one’s form is revealed throughout the entire world.
Wherever one attempts to engage in deliberation, there are a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks.
Question: Why does one who has let go on that other side not abide in the position of correctness? Answer: Great achievement is without a presiding master. Verse:
Great achievement is without a presiding master; yet the sound and light still remain. He kicks over the bed of nirvāṇa and tramples the ocean of cessation.
Holding fast and letting go, one is free at every touch. Seizing the orthodox and yielding to the biased, one merely exhausts one's spirit and brilliance.
If one can simply follow the path back home, then the days spent divining the *xiu* and *hai* palaces are in vain.
Question: Why does one who has turned their head toward this side not fall into a heterodox path? Answer: Because ultimate transformation is non-action (*wuwei*).
Verse: Ultimate transformation is non-action; the entire nation calls it marvelous. A pure breeze comes from the Purple Barrier Pass; a bright moon seals the vermilion steps.
The reality of principle is fundamentally without interval; the truth of the conventional is inherently inseparable.
Since attaining the teacherless wisdom in a single realization, he has traversed the entire Jambudvīpa without moving his feet.
Question: Why is a person who moves with seven freedoms and eight expanses, undergoing a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes, precisely the one who deserves to be struck with the staff?
Answer: It was almost let go. Verse: It was almost let go; the full transmission is entrusted. The wondrous function should be applied, and the result will surely be extraordinary.
"To see what is right and not do it is a lack of courage. Only by knowing gratitude can one repay it; this is the essence of loyalty.

One must carefully watch for the thorn in the mud on a narrow path, and skillfully preserve the awl within the empty bag. If you encounter a stubborn, dull-witted person with no blood in their veins, only then will you realize that blunt iron wastes the tongs and hammer.
Question: For one who has "finished the hundred and mastered the thousand," with what will you reward them? Answer: Zhaozhou’s tea; Caoshan’s wine. Verse:
Zhaozhou’s tea, Caoshan’s wine—no need for brewing or distilling, they are present at all times.

When thirsty, what hinders two or three cups? After sobering up, there is no harm in seven or eight *dou*. While you have not yet realized it, you laboriously serve him; I fear you will merely follow after his bitter taste.
The flavor is merely opening one’s mouth. Question:
Among the five points of Fengxue, which point is most intimate? Answer: This point is the most intimate. Verse:
This point is the most intimate; the mind is true, the words are true. It pierces open the nostrils of the monks and augments the spirit of the Buddhas and Patriarchs anew. Established.
The Dharma-banner stands upon the limit of reality; the fundamental tenet is established within a speck of dust. Countless are those who speculate with their conscious intellects;
how many are there who penetrate it directly? Question:
Among the three statements uttered by Yunmen, which one is the most wondrous? Answer: This statement is the most wondrous. Verse: This...
The phrase is most wondrous; a single word brings immediate resolution. Do not pursue right and wrong; the world is full of turmoil.
You who follow the path of Chan, apply your minds and investigate this with care. This supreme spiritual power is no small matter.
Question: The Buddha did not speak a single word; why then are his teachings said to fill the dragon palaces? Answer: Two words, three words. Verse:
Two words, three words—whether they be meaningful or meaningless—they are the true source of Prajñā, the wondrous wisdom that requires no teacher.
Behold well the yellow leaves used to stop a child’s crying; raise your eyebrows and do not hesitate to deliberate.
Question: "The cause encompasses the ocean of the fruit; the fruit reaches back to the source of the cause. But as for the phrase 'transcending cause and effect,' how do you speak of it?
Answer: "I have not yet spoken; I have not yet spoken. Verse: "I have not yet spoken; I have not yet spoken. There is no need to seek or investigate. One recognizes a person by their words;
one distinguishes weeds from the grain by the sprouts. To realize the Four Truths, there is no need for deliberation; To transcend the Ten Stages, I dare not presume."
Mutually preserving [the truth]. Question: Among the five teachings—Initial, Final, Sudden, and Perfect—is there also Chan? Answer: You have not yet understood the teachings. Verse:

If you do not yet understand the teachings, you will transcend neither the realm of conceptualization; to attempt to deliberate separately is like pouring water on the surface to stop a boiling cauldron—the Milky Way’s waves [will only rise higher].
"Though divided, the flowers of the jade grove are no different. As for 'different' and 'not different,' the clear-eyed monk merely touches upon a taboo.
Question: "The Way was told to you: 'Do not go; returning, you turn your back on your father. How can one go without turning one's back on one's father? Answer: "Above all, avoid it."
Turning Back. Verse: One must take care not to turn back; this single phrase is extraordinary. How many people know the profound mysteries within it?
If you can simply proceed without self-interest beneath your feet, the Bird Path will be traversed freely, and all places will be suitable.

Question: "Responding to conditions and meeting with sentient beings, there is nowhere he does not reach; yet he always remains upon this seat of Bodhi. Now tell me, where exactly is this seat of Bodhi?
Answer: "It is not that which is being spoken of. Verse: "It is not that which is being spoken of"—do not treat this too casually.
Bricks, pebbles, thorns, and brambles—none are not the most precious treasure. The wondrous essence is beyond dependence; a single phrase of mystery pervades as many lands as there are motes of dust.
Master Tan asked:
"The wondrous flowers of Bodhi are everywhere adorning; wherever they dwell, there is constant peace and joy. Where, then, are these wondrous flowers of Bodhi? He replied:
"When one has sold all their elegance and charm for no price. Verse: When one has sold all their elegance and charm for no price.
Those who know the sound need not have it proclaimed again; Śūnyatā-janman has grown accustomed to the commonplace. These starving-eyed Chan practitioners are even more pitiable.
Question: "Hearing the bell, one ascends the jeweled hall; striking the drum, one enters the void. Is this not the gate through which Avalokiteśvara enters into principle?"
Answer: In a low voice, in a low voice. Verse: Presented in a low voice, it is not at all obscure. Is there no resentment? Are you weary of this life? Have you understood?
The moon in the ocean of the vows of compassion and wisdom; the wind-stirred branches of the wisdom derived from hearing, contemplation, and cultivation. Du Chanhe.
Do not let the moment slip away. Following sounds and pursuing forms—what is the ultimate result? Question:
For one who has severed attachments and resolved all doubts, who has penetrated through sound and form to clarify the mind and see the nature—is such a person ultimately thorough or not?
Answer: The hook is caught in the ground of non-doubt. Verse: The hook is caught in the ground of non-doubt; delusion and enlightenment, right and wrong, are of one essence. When...
In his declining years, Xuansha was once playfully rebuffed by Lingyun: "You boast of being 'clearly and perfectly enlightened,' but I say you are merely fast asleep.
Do not sleep! After the rain has fallen and the clouds have cleared, the mountains grow ever more verdant.
Question: "Birth is like putting on a shirt; death is like taking off one's trousers. What principle has such a person attained?
Answer: "Empty-handed and bare-fisted. Verse: Empty-handed and bare-fisted, there is nothing in all things; One must further let go and return to the path.
If you can accept and take this up in this way, Then you will believe that the Master’s virtue is not in vain. Virtue is not in vain—do not be vague!
Every person has ten thousand measures of provisions; one need only fear that at the critical moment they prove no man of substance. Question:
The past has already ceased, the future has not yet arrived, and the present is empty and still.

Why then, when adverse or favorable circumstances manifest before you, are you unable to penetrate them? Answer: It is because you recognize pain and itchiness. Verse: It is because you recognize pain and itchiness.

I decline not to receive your praise and encouragement. My dream from yesterday has just awakened; right and wrong belong to the past. The Buddhas and Patriarchs’ provisional teachings rest upon Wansong;
do not follow mere words and phrases in vain agitation.
Question: "The learned abandon that which is meaningless; the learned understand the Dharma. Now tell me, what kind of Dharma do they understand? Answer:

This meaning is extensive in its textual expression. Verse: This meaning is extensive in its textual expression; one must strictly avoid deliberation upon it. It is not like a fly boring into old paper.
How could this be the same as boring through and warding off broken fragments? You clever fellows, do not be reckless! The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands is difficult to grasp;
the Child Who Speaks No Words excels at proclaiming it.
Question: I have a single phrase that clarifies the ten mysterious gates and the meaning of the six aspects (*ṣaḷlakṣaṇa*).
Is there anyone who can express it? Answer: Withdraw. Verse: Withdraw. Cutting off all currents, the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are peerless and without equal.
When the chrysanthemums bloom, the Double Ninth arrives; when a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the world.
Question: Without stopping at the conjured city, one goes straight to the treasure place. Tell me, where is that treasure place? Answer:
There is not even two taels of gold here. Verse: "There is not even two taels of gold here" is much like raising one's voice to silence the echo;
the pearl within the robe is clearly manifest, yet one merely continues to wander aimlessly. If they further intend to remain ignorant of its location, then— [The master] strikes them with his staff.
Lansai struck him once with his palm and asked, "All phenomena that possess marks are entirely illusory; which one is the true reality? He replied, "Do not engage in false conceptualization.
Verse: Do not engage in false conceptualization; there is nothing further to be contrived. If you wish to know the perfect fusion of the real and the illusory, recognize Bodhi.
Grasping at afflictions—greed, anger, and delusion—is nothing other than the Way. To calculate otherwise and seek it elsewhere is in vain.
Question: "All bodies are entirely impure; how then is one to account for the thirty-two marks of a Buddha?
Answer: "Shatter the painted vase! Verse: Shatter the painted vase, And like a drunkard suddenly sobering up, The sixteen-foot golden body Manifests to mark all things.
The autumn waters are as pure as a monk’s azure eyes; the morning mountains are as dense as a Buddha’s azure head.
Question: "The Chan school is divided into five branches. Is there any distinction of superiority or inferiority among them? Answer: "If they were inferior, they would all be equally inferior.

Verse: If they were inferior, they would all be equally inferior; They cannot be distinguished. A jar and a bowl, hairpins and bracelets— Their substance is the same, though their names differ. This is already perfect penetration.
Too much talk! Who can endure Yaoshan’s loquacity? I shall decide it for you: on the sixth month, wherever the sun shines, it is hot. Question:
"When the teachings arrange the Three Vehicles, is there still victory or defeat? Answer: "If there is victory, all are victorious. Verse:
"If there is victory, all are victorious; For them, it is personal realization. The Buddha and Patriarchs' scale and balance— Is it fixed or not fixed? Nevertheless, it does not accord with..."
"You share the same scale; when it comes to the final weight, it is difficult for the balance to be deceived.
Question: "Are there differences in depth between the two schools of Nature (Xing) and Characteristics (Xiang)? Answer: "The one who seeks the distinct must first exhaust [the inquiry]. Verse:

Seeking another path first, the common person exhausts their efforts; the circular and the sequential are forcibly made to appear fragmented. Look closely at the division of fields and the separation of waterways:
when a family is in discord, the neighbors will exploit them.
Question: How are the four ailments of striving, ceasing, indulgence, and extinction to be treated? Answer: Each of these aforementioned cases requires equal proportions.
Verse: Each of the aforementioned cases requires equal proportions. Having received your precious instructions, a single pill cures the ailment and brings peace. Why rely on a donkey for transport?
With the faces of the sun and moon, I respond to the times; who would fear repeated inquiries?
Question: There is only the one true moon; in between, there is nothing that is neither moon nor non-moon.

How, then, is this the true moon? Answer: Where is its pure radiance not present? Verse: Where is its pure radiance not present? Wondrous Virtue turns the profound pivot. Deeply serene, the golden ripples are cool;
motionless, the jade hare stands alone. Even a curved hook cannot compare to it; a bright mirror is even more distinct. If you understand...
When Yunyan held up his broom, the meaning was that one must know it fundamentally requires no effort.
Question: When Vimalakīrti remained silent to discourse on non-duality, how should later generations propagate this? Answer: Thank the Master for piercing through [the mystery].
Verse: Thank the Master for piercing through; both have fallen into speech. Who would have thought that today yet another has been added? It is like—
This proclaims the vehicle of the school; it makes even the Great King of the Eastern Village laugh to death.
Question: "The Buddha’s words take the mind as their essence. I do not yet know what the mind takes as its essence. Answer: What is there that it does not take as its essence?
Verse: What is there that is not honored? Every single thing follows [this principle]. Perfectly realized in a single thought-moment, wondrous virtue is most majestic.
It is all like Sadāprarudita selling everything; one must know that stagnant water does not harbor dragons.
Question: "The gateless is the Dharma-gate. Tell me, how does one enter? Answer: "Who is outside the gate?
Verse: Who is outside the gate? Heaven and earth are not large. The monastery of Perfect Enlightenment has long been refined and purified.
There is no need to carry a staff to knock at the moon; once the City of Transformation is broken through, there is no obstruction.
Question: You have recorded that one who has the "original character" (yuan-zi-jiao) in their heart acts as a wild fox spirit.
But what does one do who lacks this original character? Answer: There is yet another, the red-bearded fox. Verse: There is yet another, the red-bearded fox; alas for the talisman on the elbow!

Sentient consciousness exists as it truly is; cause and effect are not non-existent. Skillful like the clumsy, wise like the foolish—how many... (Note: The final line appears to be an incomplete fragment.)
Such a man is a true hero. Question:
To utter the two words "Buddha-dharma" is to rinse one’s mouth clean for three days. Tell me, where does the fault of the Buddha-dharma lie? Answer:
Simply swallow what you have spat out and spit it back up again. Verse: Simply swallow what you have spat out and spit it back up again; How many can see through this?
Mahāsūtra. Namo samantān. Samantān. This means that throughout the world, one has no verbal transgressions. Question:
Regarding the phrase "the separate transmission outside the teachings" of the Patriarchs, I ask you, Zen practitioner, to reveal it to me. Answer: Mahalla.
The *gueduo* (peacock-feather whisk). A verse: The *mahallaka-gueduo* (the elder’s whisk) was not yet fully approved.

Standing in the snow and picking up the flower—both have already met with derision (*mlāna*). Not sparing even his eyebrows, he tells you to know: when hot, seek the cool; when cold, turn toward the fire.
Question: "The path of Stonehead is slippery; it is difficult for people to pass. How does one proceed by the side of the Green Jade Stream?
Answer: (He) picks up his staff. Verse: Picking up the staff, he walks slowly away. Within the city of Gandharva, atop the crown of Vairocana.
The path of Stonehead is slippery—beyond effort. The road by the Jade Stream is vast—beyond thought.
Question: "Delightfully dwelling in the mountains, sleeping in leisure, one’s dreams are not startled. Tell me, what did you see in your dream?
Answer: "Mumbling in one's sleep. Verse: "Mumbling in one's sleep; the Kingdom of Huaxu is shattered and there is no place of reliance. Xiangyan and Jizang were far too vague.
Water for washing and tea were offered, praying for permission."
Question: Yunju said, "Living in the mountains is good. But tell me, where is it good? Answer: At the summit of Tongxuan Peak. Verse:
At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, naturally solitary and remote. If you attempt to travel there, your legs will be broken by my whip.
Great recluses dwell in the marketplace; small recluses dwell in the mountains. Adapting to people and shifting with circumstances, they are both without equal.
Question: “My teacher has been outside the ‘Rain of Flowers’ [monastery] for more than ten years. What has he been doing all this time in these mountains?
Answer: “He has many years but no virtue. Verse: Having many years but no virtue, he does not conform to rules or regulations; he points east when it is west.
To call south north is merely a matter of comparing the states of exhaustion and penetration; viewed with the correct eye, it still requires effort. Question:
"At this time, the mountain monk does not understand at all. Is this understanding and yet not understanding? Or is it neither understanding nor non-understanding? Answer:
"Have you met the Master yet? The verse says: "Have you met the Master yet? He plays with the vapors of rice and gruel; he wondrously turns the celestial wheel and the terrestrial axis.
He secretly weaves the civil classics as warp and the martial arts as woof. The great uncut jade is pure and true; the perfect pearl is more precious for being unpierced."

Question: It is not difficult to know; it is only the practice that is hard. Now tell me, how does one practice? Answer: I ask the Master to lead the way first. Verse: I ask the Master to lead the way first;
do not dwell on the contrary or the compliant. Simply ask, shatter the precarious, and gather what is accomplished.
Do not speak of good fortune, misfortune, regret, or gain. The Great Way runs lengthwise and crosswise, inherently level; why need one wear the Seal of the Empty King at the waist?
Question: Because they have not yet reached the source of the Dharma, there is much contention and debate. Is there anyone who has thoroughly penetrated the source of the Dharma?
Answer: He overturns the meditation cushion. Verse: Overturning the meditation cushion, he reveals the great capacity; how many can here penetrate the profound mystery?
Having exhausted the source of the Dharma to its very bottom, one suddenly realizes that the void has diminished in girth.
Question: That which is luminously clear and not obscure, that which is always knowing and ever-present—what is this? Answer: A ghost’s eye. Verse:
What a fine, brilliant ghost’s eye! It spies out all right and wrong, yet there is neither gain nor loss.
How much better to remain in a state of dull, ignorant stillness, and simply become brothers with the brow’s edge.
Question: How are Buddha-nature and Dharma-nature to be distinguished? Answer: We shall discuss this again on another day. Verse:
We shall discuss this again on another day; with compassion, I raise it up for you. I spare not even my eyebrows; how could the path of thought conceal it?

At night, the moonlight extends across the water; at dawn, the shadows of the morning sun shift along the corridors. At the place where the Jade Brook provides instruction, one should investigate and deliberate with subtle care.
Question: Regarding traveling far and traveling in accordance [with the Way], tell me, how does one distinguish between them? Answer: Do you have eyes? Verse:
Is there still an eye? A single word encompasses all—clear and luminous. An arrow piercing the red target: hearing sounds and observing forms are both suchness (*tathatā*).
Whether in opposition or accord, they all return to the same; nothing is not permissible.
Question: If the virtues of one's nature are inherently present, why is there no awakening or knowledge of them? Answer: One has almost forgotten them. Verse:
Almost forgotten, yet for the sake of responding to others, the numinous clarity within the heart-mind—how could it have come from a "heavenly rank"?
To understand it in such a way is a thousand errors, ten thousand errors. If you wish not to err, stop trying to lengthen the crane by cutting off its neck or shorten the duck by adding to its body.
Question: Emotions and delusions are fundamentally empty; why then do they follow sound and pursue form? Answer: A verse by a monk who has attained universal mastery:
A monk who has attained universal mastery is truly brilliant; His eyes and ears are unimpeded in seeing and hearing. How could the bright moon ever leave the azure autumn waters?
How could floating clouds obstruct the green morning peaks? Within sound and form, he is intoxicated and yet awakened; The six states of existence remain tranquil.
Ben-zin-nei asked:
"A bhikṣu dwells relying upon the four foundations of mindfulness; upon what basis does a person of great icchantika-dharma dwell? He replied:

"Within the path of uninterrupted realization (ānantarya-mārga). Verse: Within the path of uninterrupted realization, from west to east, one is not yet thoroughly liberated; there is no enjoyment [of the fruit].
Exhausted. Have you not seen that Devadatta once said: "The bliss of the third dhyāna heaven is ultimately not the same"?
Question: Is there still any contradiction between the Mahāyāna and the Hīnayāna? Answer: One has many aspects. Verse:
There are many kinds of peaks here; their ridges soar upward, brushing against the heavens and reaching into the void. Even Mount Sumeru would feel abashed before them.
In days to come, this "Blow-Off-Sword" shall take its rightful place, surely pruning away the profusion and redundancy of the human world.
Question: Is there any mutual accord between the true mind and the deluded mind? Answer: There are not two, nor are they two distinct segments. Verse:
There are not two, nor are they two distinct segments; I do not dare to deceive you. Suchness and wondrous wisdom are like a pearl rolling upon a tray.
If you can perfect this single thought-moment, cease seeking out myriad threads and a thousand ends.
Question: How are the three subtleties and six coarsenesses to be distinguished? Answer: I have never drafted a public proclamation. [Verse: I have never drafted a public proclamation;
karma, the evolving consciousness, and manifestation are all entrusted [to you]. This meaning is extensive in text and shall be proclaimed on another day;
for now, I follow the path that awakens the vital spirit within the Zen Garden.

After winter, one counts nine days for each subsequent year.
Question: [The Master] held up one finger and said, "Master Juzhi emits great radiance and turns the Great Dharma Wheel right here.
Do you all see it? Answer: "Blind! Verse: How could the blind know that the eyes are doubly bright? Subtle...
The scroll of the *Dhūli-sūtra* concludes a lifetime; on the tip of a finger, there is but a tiny bit. How many days of travel can this master endure?
Question: Using a broken-legged cauldron as one’s livelihood, making a pierced-heart bowl one’s way of life—where does one rest within the Tongxuan Hermitage?
Yet he sits there, unconcerned with the affairs before the mountain that are as numerous as hemp seeds. But tell me, who is this person who remains so at ease?
Answer: A man who receives his emolument without merit. Verse: A man who receives his emolument without merit; The moon is his neighbor and the clouds his companions.
When hungry he eats, when thirsty he drinks, and when weary he sleeps; Beyond this, there is no need for idle praise.
Question: "Non-seeking is bliss. Why then did Prince Shan-you seek the pearl? Answer: "Calamity arises from the private door.
Verse: Calamity arises from the private door; it happens of its own accord. Do not falsely probe with conceptual consciousness. White clouds cross the valley, unfolding and then rolling back;
how could they obstruct the clear sky or the profound heavens? (This twentieth question was lost previously and is supplemented here.)
The Hundred Questions on Penetrating the Profundities (End)
